Smooths lines with the sliding averaging of McMaster: each vertex moves towards the average of the vertices around it.

**Toolbox folder:** Vector Processing<br>
**Status:** Certified<br>
**Keywords:** Smoothing, Vector, Generalization<br>
**Authors:** Andrea Antonello<br>
**Class:** `org.hortonmachine.modules.LineSmootherMcMaster`

**Inputs**

| Parameter | Type | Unit | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `inVector` | vector file |  |  | The vector containing the lines to be smoothed. |
| `pLookahead` | int |  | `7` | The number of vertices averaged for each vertex, an odd number (default = 7). |
| `pLimit` | int |  | `0` | The length up to which the lines are not smoothed: of them, the closed ones and the ones not connected to other lines are removed. |
| `pSlide` | double |  | `0.9` | How far each vertex moves towards the average, from 0 (it stays) to 1 (it goes to the average). |
| `pDensify` | Double |  |  | The optional maximum distance between the vertices, added before the smoothing. |
| `pSimplify` | Double |  |  | The optional tolerance of a simplification after the smoothing. |

**Outputs**

| Parameter | Type | Unit | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `outVector` | output file |  | The vector with smoothed features. |

**References**

- McMaster, R. B. (1989). The integration of simplification and smoothing algorithms in line generalization. Cartographica, 26(1), 101-121.
